r0.why: Fine-grained extrusive rock from fast-cooled low-viscosity Mg/Fe-rich lava at or near surface [1]; over 90% of volcanic rock [2]; upper-mantle origin and chemistry as clue [9][10].

r1.why: Silica 45-52%, low viscosity, fast wide-spreading flows [7]; 10^4-10^5 cP, ketchup, water 1 cP [24]; flood basalts thick, hundreds of thousands of km2, most voluminous [8].

r2.why: Decompression melting [36]; pressure raises melting point so upper mantle mostly solid [37]; ductile [38]; upward creep lowers pressure and melting point giving partial melt [39].

r3.why: Four settings listed in [40]; subduction mantle wedge [41]; slab volatiles lower melting point and increase melting [42]; distinctive characteristics per setting [43].

r4.why: Dark colour from augite/pyroxene [19]; light ones from plagioclase [20]; phenocrysts formed before extrusion in finer matrix [25]; vesicles from degassing [27]; scoria [28].

r5.why: Gabbro same composition and mineralogy, slow-cooling and coarse [3]; important on other bodies [5]; Venus plains ~80%, lunar maria, Mars [6].
